summary: Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and under Stewart Sutherland, Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, Prithwish Neogy, Rama Nath Sharma, and Kashi Nath Upadhyaya.

Frank J. Korom works in religious studies and Indology. He studied as a graduate student at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 1990) and held a post as professor at Boston University (attested 2005).

Frank Lee Woodward worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Christ's Hospital and Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge (~1890–1902), and under Caroline Rhys Davids (~1914–1942). He held posts at Mahinda College (1903–1919) and the Pali Text Society (~1914–1919).

Frank-Richard Hamm was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring (1940–1948) and at the International Academy of Indian Culture. He held posts at Hamburg (1948–1952, 1957–1964) and the University of Bonn (1965).

Franklin Edgerton studied at Cornell, Munich, Jena, and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, Hermann Collitz, and others. Specializing in Indology and linguistics, he held professorships at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Yale University (1926–1953).

Franz Altheim studied at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1919–1928), working in linguistics, archaeology, history, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Frankfurt (~1928–1943), the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1943–1950), and the Free University of Berlin (~1950–1964).

Franz Aubrey Metcalf specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago and served as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 2002–2006).

Franz Bernhard was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt at Göttingen (~1954–1959) and habilitated at Frankfurt (~1960–1965). From 1966 to 1971, he was professor and seminar director at the University of Hamburg.

Franz Boas studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, Kiel, and under Wilhelm Wundt. He worked in linguistics and related fields, holding posts at the Smithsonian Institution (~1885–1886), Clark University (~1889–1892), the American Museum of Natural History (1896–1900), and Columbia University (~1896–1936).

Franz Bopp studied in Paris under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, as well as in London and Göttingen. A specialist in linguistics and Indology, he held the Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Berlin from 1821 to 1867.

Franz Heinrich Trithen was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Berlin under Franz Bopp (1838–1840). He later held posts at the British Museum (~1844–1848) and the University of Oxford (~1848–1854).

Franz Kielhorn studied at Göttingen, Breslau, and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Albrecht Weber, and Theodor Benfey. A specialist in Indology and linguistics, he held posts at Deccan College (1866–1881) and the University of Göttingen (from 1881).
Franz Xaver Erhard is a scholar of Tibetology. He completed an MA at the Free University of Berlin and the University of Berlin, and earned his PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

Franz von Erdmann studied at the University of Rostock (~1814–1817). A scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics, he held a post at Kazan Imperial University from approximately 1818 to 1845.

Franz-Karl Ehrhard studied at Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. A specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he served as Resident Representative for the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993) and held a professorship at the University of Munich (2001–2019).
François Grimal is an Indologist who held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and served as Director at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (~2002–2006).

François Gros was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon (~1951–1956). He served as Directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1977–2002) and was a reading committee member for Collection Indologie (attested 2004).
François Lachaud is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who held posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, where he was attested as professor in 2008 and affiliated in 2013.

Françoise Pommaret, a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology, studied at the Sorbonne, INALCO, and the University of Paris. She held posts at INALCO (~1979), CNRS (from 2002), and the Royal University of Bhutan (~2008), and directed Langues et cultures de l'aire tibétaine.

Françoise Robin studied at INALCO under Heather Stoddard, specializing in Tibetology and linguistics. She served as a director at the Collège de France (2009–2015) and held departmental leadership posts at INALCO (2011, 2013–2014).
